A medical wound-healing accelerator is disclosed. According to an embodiment of the present invention, the medical wound-healing accelerator comprises: a body removably attachable to a fixing pin of an external fracture fixator, the fixing pin being inserted through the skin into a bone; a plurality of light-source units arranged on one lateral surface of the body and configured to irradiate the skin with light that has a beneficial effect on a wound; and a controller electrically connected to the light-source units and configured to control their operation.

Additionally, an osteomyelitis treatment device comprises: an insert configured to be inserted into an osteomyelitis-affected region of the human body; and a plurality of light-emitting members provided on the insert and configured to emit light. The light-emitting members are spaced apart from one another along the longitudinal direction of the insert, and the portion of the insert along which the light-emitting members are spaced apart may be cut or bent to conform to the shape of the osteomyelitis-affected region.

A medical device designed to promote wound repair is described. In one embodiment, the device includes a main body removably mounted on a fixation pin of a fracture external fixator, with the pin extending through the skin and into a bone. Multiple light-source modules are positioned along one side of the main body and direct wound-healing light toward the skin. A controller is electrically coupled to the light-source modules and regulates their operation.

An apparatus for treating osteomyelitis is also provided. The apparatus has an insert configured for placement within an osteomyelitis-affected region of the human body and multiple light-emitting elements mounted on the insert. These elements are separated from one another along the insert’s longitudinal axis. The section of the insert containing the spaced light-emitting elements may be cut or bent to conform to the shape of the affected region.

The fixation pin is inserted through the patient’s skin and into a bone. Multiple light-source units are arranged on one side of the body and configured to emit light that promotes healing of the wound surrounding the pin. outputs.L4:
The disclosure describes light-based medical devices designed to promote localized healing in patients with external fixation hardware or bone infections. In one embodiment, a wound-healing accelerator is mounted on a pin of an external fixator so that one or more light sources can be positioned near a skin wound, such as the tissue surrounding the pin-entry site. A controller operates the light sources and may regulate treatment parameters such as activation timing, duration, intensity, or illumination sequence. By using the existing fixation pin as a mounting point, the device can maintain a stable relationship with the treatment area while delivering therapeutic light directly to the affected tissue.

The disclosure also presents an insert intended for the treatment of osteomyelitis. The insert includes multiple light emitters arranged at spaced locations along an elongated or otherwise adaptable supporting structure. The structure can be cut to a selected length, bent, or shaped to conform to a bone cavity, surgical site, or infected region. This adjustability allows clinicians to distribute the emitters throughout the area requiring treatment rather than illuminating only a single surface location.

In use, the insert may be positioned within or adjacent to an osteomyelitis site so that therapeutic light is delivered close to infected bone and surrounding tissue. The spacing of the emitters can provide broader and more uniform coverage, while the cuttable or bendable construction permits customization for different anatomical geometries and treatment needs. The controller-operated external-fixator device and the adaptable osteomyelitis insert therefore provide targeted light delivery at locations that may be difficult to treat effectively using conventional external illumination.

Together, these devices offer flexible platforms for localized phototherapy. Direct placement near a wound or infection site may reduce losses associated with light passing through intervening tissue and may improve the consistency of treatment. As a result, the disclosed systems have the potential to support wound repair, assist in managing bone infections, and enhance treatment effectiveness while accommodating patient-specific anatomy and clinical requirements.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for a light-based medical wound healing accelerator attachable to an external fracture fixator pin, and an insertable osteomyelitis treatment device with spaced light emitters.
counterfactuals.output: A phototherapeutic system for treating wounds and bone infections includes a light delivery device configured for attachment to an external fracture-fixator pin. The device includes a housing, a pin-engagement member, and one or more light emitters oriented to direct therapeutic light toward tissue surrounding a pin-entry site, thereby promoting wound healing and reducing microbial burden. The system may further include an elongate device insertable into a bone cavity or medullary canal for treatment of osteomyelitis. The elongate device includes a biocompatible body carrying a plurality of light emitters spaced along its length to distribute therapeutic light within the infected region. A controller may regulate wavelength, intensity, duty cycle, and treatment duration for the emitters. The devices may employ antimicrobial, photobiomodulatory, or photosensitizer-activating wavelengths and may include sensors, wireless communication circuitry, and a rechargeable or external power source.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention that uses phototherapy to promote healing around fixation pins and treat osteomyelitis inside the body.
counterfactuals.output:
### Dual-Mode Phototherapy Fixation Pin System

The invention is an orthopedic fixation pin that also delivers light therapy to the pin tract and infected bone. It combines **photobiomodulation** to support healing with **antimicrobial photodynamic therapy** to treat osteomyelitis.

**Main components**

- **Cannulated fixation pin:** A hollow, biocompatible metal or reinforced polymer pin containing an optical fiber.
- **External light collar:** A sterile ring surrounding the skin entry site that illuminates the pin tract to reduce inflammation, encourage tissue repair, and suppress surface infection.
- **Internal light diffuser:** Side-emitting windows or a cylindrical diffuser near the pin tip deliver light directly into the medullary cavity or infected bone.
- **Photosensitizer delivery channel:** An optional lumen introduces a locally administered antimicrobial photosensitizer into infected tissue.
- **Programmable controller:** Selects wavelength, intensity, pulse pattern, and treatment duration while monitoring temperature and delivered dose.

**Operation**

For osteomyelitis treatment, a photosensitizer is introduced into the affected bone and activated with red or near-infrared light. Activation produces short-lived reactive oxygen species that damage bacteria and biofilms locally. A lower-intensity photobiomodulation mode is then used around the pin tract and fracture site to promote cellular energy production, vascularization, and wound repair.

Temperature, optical output, and treatment history are monitored to prevent thermal injury. Replaceable sterile collars allow repeated bedside treatments without removing the fixation pin. The device is intended as an adjunct—not a replacement—for debridement, stabilization, and systemic or local antibiotics, and would require clinical validation and regulatory approval.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a formal patent-style summary of two related medical devices: one with detachable light sources mounted on an external fixator pin, and another flexible or cuttable insert containing multiple longitudinally spaced light-emitting members.
counterfactuals.output:
Disclosed are related medical illumination devices configured to deliver light to tissue at or adjacent to a treatment site. In a first aspect, a medical device includes an external fixation pin configured for placement through or into a patient’s anatomy and one or more light-source modules removably coupled to an externally accessible portion of the pin. The light-source modules may be selectively attached, detached, replaced, or repositioned without removing the pin and may direct therapeutic light through the pin, along the pin, or toward tissue surrounding an implanted portion of the pin.

In a second aspect, a medical device includes an elongate insert configured for placement within, alongside, or around an anatomical structure. The insert is flexible, trimmable, or otherwise cuttable to accommodate a selected treatment geometry and includes a plurality of light-emitting members spaced apart in a longitudinal direction. The light-emitting members may be independently or collectively energized to provide distributed illumination along at least a portion of the insert. Associated conductors, optical elements, control circuitry, and a power source may be incorporated into or coupled to the insert. The disclosed devices thereby permit configurable delivery of light over localized or extended treatment regions while facilitating adaptation to patient anatomy and clinical requirements.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a concise technical disclosure for a wound-healing apparatus comprising a pin-mounted body, skin-directed light source units, and a controller, plus an osteomyelitis implant whose illuminated section can be bent or trimmed to fit the affected area.
counterfactuals.output:
### Technical Disclosure

A wound-healing apparatus includes a body configured for attachment to one or more percutaneous fixation pins adjacent to a wound. The body supports multiple skin-directed light-source units, each oriented to irradiate a selected skin or wound region. A controller independently or collectively regulates the light-source units according to programmed parameters including wavelength, irradiance, pulse pattern, treatment duration, and delivered optical dose. The body may provide adjustable positioning while maintaining clearance from the wound and may include temperature or optical-feedback sensors for dose and safety control.

An osteomyelitis-treatment implant includes a biocompatible illuminated section configured for placement within or adjacent to an infected bone cavity. The illuminated section comprises distributed emitters or a light-transmitting structure coupled to an external or implanted light source. At least part of the illuminated section is bendable, plastically deformable, and/or trimmable so that its geometry and length can be adapted intraoperatively to the affected area while preserving optical delivery. The controller may operate the implant alone or together with the skin-directed light-source units to administer predetermined phototherapeutic treatment protocols.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following invention concept into patent language: LEDs around an external fixation pin irradiate the skin to accelerate wound healing, while a customizable insert with multiple spaced LEDs delivers therapeutic light directly to an osteomyelitis site.
counterfactuals.output:
### Patent-Style Description

A phototherapeutic system for use with an external fixation apparatus comprises an external fixation pin configured to extend through a patient’s skin and into a bone, and a first plurality of light-emitting diodes disposed circumferentially about the pin adjacent to a skin-entry site. The first plurality of light-emitting diodes is configured to irradiate tissue surrounding the skin-entry site with light having one or more therapeutic wavelengths to promote wound healing and/or reduce microbial burden.

The system further comprises a customizable insert sized and shaped for positioning within or adjacent to an osteomyelitis site. The insert includes a second plurality of light-emitting diodes arranged at spaced locations along the insert and configured to deliver therapeutic light directly to infected bone or surrounding tissue. The geometry, LED spacing, wavelength, intensity, and irradiation schedule of the insert may be selected based on the dimensions and anatomical configuration of the treatment site.

A controller may independently control the first and second pluralities of light-emitting diodes to provide continuous, pulsed, sequential, or otherwise modulated irradiation according to a predetermined treatment protocol.

### Exemplary Independent Claim

1. **A phototherapeutic external fixation system comprising:**  
   an external fixation pin configured to pass through skin and engage a bone of a patient;  
   a first plurality of light-emitting elements positioned around the external fixation pin and configured to irradiate tissue surrounding a percutaneous entry site of the external fixation pin;  
   an insert configured to be positioned within or adjacent to an osteomyelitis treatment site, the insert comprising a second plurality of light-emitting elements spaced apart from one another and configured to irradiate bone or tissue at the osteomyelitis treatment site; and  
   a controller operatively coupled to the first plurality of light-emitting elements and the second plurality of light-emitting elements and configured to control delivery of therapeutic light thereto.

### Exemplary Dependent Claims

2. The system of claim 1, wherein the first plurality of light-emitting elements is arranged circumferentially about the external fixation pin.

3. The system of claim 1, wherein the insert is patient-specific and has a geometry selected according to imaging data defining the osteomyelitis treatment site.

4. The system of claim 1, wherein the second plurality of light-emitting elements is distributed longitudinally, circumferentially, or three-dimensionally throughout the insert.

5. The system of claim 1, wherein the controller independently controls wavelength, irradiance, pulse duration, duty cycle, or treatment duration for the first and second pluralities of light-emitting elements.

6. The system of claim 1, wherein at least one of the first or second pluralities of light-emitting elements emits visible, red, near-infrared, ultraviolet, or combinations thereof.

7. The system of claim 1, wherein the insert is removable, biocompatible, sterilizable, resorbable, or additively manufactured.

8. The system of claim 1, further comprising one or more sensors configured to detect temperature, optical dose, tissue oxygenation, microbial activity, or inflammation at the percutaneous entry site or the osteomyelitis treatment site.
